ACCREDITATION AND ACADEMIC CALENDARS
Florida State University is a fully accredited member of the Southern
Association of Colleges and Schools, and thereby is accredited for the
Southern region, and reciprocally, for the country.
Florida State University College of Medicine was accredited by the Liaison
Committ ee on Medical Education of the Association of American Medical
Colleges and the American Medical Association, February 4, 2005.
Florida State College for Women (1909 - 1947) by act of the 1947 Florida
State Legislature was made a co - educational institut ion and designated
“Florida State University.” The unit of credit at that time was the quarter hour
and term designation was Quarter.
Effective September, 1951 – The academic calendar for Florida State
University was divided into two equal terms and a summer session, thereby
having semester hours as the unit of credit.
Effective September, 1962 – The academic calendar for Florida State
University was divided into three equal terms, the unit of credit was semester;
and the term designation was Tri mester.
Effective September, 1967 – The academic calendar for Florida State
University reverted to four terms and the unit of credit was designated the
quarter hour.
Effe ctive August , 1981 – The academic calendar for Florida State
University reve rted to two equal terms and a summer session and the unit of
credit was semester hours.
Effective August, 1984 – Florida State University implemented a grading
system in which pluses and minuses may be added to the traditional letter
grades.

QUALITY POINTS
Prior to the Fall Semester, 1955, the University operated on a three point
grade system. However, from Fall Semester, 1955 to Fall 1984 quality points
were assigned to passing grades as follows: A: 4 q.p.; B: 3 q.p.; C: 2 q.p.;
D: 1 q.p.; F: 0 q.p.; IE: 0 q.p.; GE: 0 q.p.
Effective Fall Semester, 1984, quality points are assigned to grades
earned as follows: A: 4.00 q.p.; A - : 3.75 q.p.; B+: 3.25 q.p.; B: 3.00 q.p.; B -
The grade point average is computed by dividing the number of hours
attempted with letter grades (A, B, C, D, F, IE, and GE) at Florida State
University into the total number of quality points assigned.
Effective Spring Quarter, 1971, the University i nstituted a “forgiveness”
policy for undergraduate students which permitted said students to repeat
grades of “D” and “F” in order to improve their leve l of performance (g.p.a.);
the last attempt only is computed in the average.
Effective Spring Quarter, 1974, the University instituted a “forgiveness”
policy for graduate students which permitted said students to repeat grades
of “C” or below in order to improve their level of performance (g.p.a.). This
option could be exercised for no more than two courses and only once for any
particular course.
Effective Fall Quarter, 1980, both undergraduate and graduate students
were also limited to two repeat s under the forgiveness policy for the purpose
of improving the g.p.a.
Effective Summer 2003, the College of Medicine instituted grades of
Honors Medicine (HM), 4.00 q.p. and Pass Medicine (PM) , 3.00 q.p.
Effective Fall 2004, the forgiveness polic y was discontinued.
Effective Fall 2022, the College of Law quality points are assigned to grades as
q.p .
Effective Summer 2023, the College of Medicine instituted a grade of High Pass
Medicine (HP ), 3.5 0 q.p.

COURSE NUMBERING SYSTEM
Effective September, 1978, prefixes and numbers appear according to the Common
Course Number designations implemented by the State Department of Education. The first
digit of the 4 - digit number represents the level of the course (0, introductory, coll ege prep:
1, 2 lower level; 3, 4 upper level; 5, 6 graduate level: 7, 8, 9 graduate and professional)
and is assigned by Florida State University . The second digit represents the major
subclassification of the discipline, i.e., 0, introductory, entry level course; 9, miscellaneous
general categories such as thesis and seminars. The third and fourth digits are used for
indicating level of complexity and for sequencing. The outside indicator “L” means that the
course is a laboratory course, the “C” means that the course is a combination of lecture
and laboratory.

GRADUATION REQUIREMENTS
Undergraduate: 120 semester hours minimum for all degrees and a minimum
cumulative 2.00 g.p.a. on all college hours attempted.
Graduate: For master’s degree, 30 semester hours, minimum, with additional credit,
thesis, etc. subject to specific dep artmental requirements and a minimum cumulative 3.00
g.p.a. on all college hours attempted. For doctoral degrees, completion of 30 semester
hours of graduate work or award of the master’s degree, after which the student must be
cont inuously enrolled on Flo rida State University c ampus or in one of its teaching centers,
for a minimum of 24 semester credit hours during one academic year; and a minimum
cumulative 3.00 g.p.a. on all college hours attempted.
